title: Index funds, expense ratio and direct vs regular plans
publisher: Artha Kavach summary of public guidance (RBI / SEBI / IRDAI / Income Tax Dept) — pending manual verification
text: An index fund simply copies a market index such as Nifty 50 or Sensex, so it has no manager trying to beat the market and costs very little. Every mutual fund charges an annual fee called the expense ratio, deducted from your returns. Index funds often charge around 0.1–0.5% a year, while actively managed funds can charge 1–2% or more. Every fund also has a 'Direct' plan (you buy straight from the fund house, no distributor commission) and a 'Regular' plan (a distributor is paid out of the fund). Direct plans have a lower expense ratio, which over 15–20 years can add up to a noticeably bigger corpus. Low cost is one of the few things in investing you can actually control.
summary_hinglish: Index fund Nifty 50 ya Sensex ko copy karta hai, isliye kharcha (expense ratio) bahut kam hota hai. Direct plan mein distributor ka commission nahi katta, to lambe time mein zyada paisa bachta hai.
summary_hi: इंडेक्स फंड निफ्टी 50 या सेंसेक्स की नकल करता है, इसलिए खर्च (एक्सपेंस रेशियो) कम होता है। डायरेक्ट प्लान में डिस्ट्रीब्यूटर का कमीशन नहीं कटता, इसलिए लंबे समय में ज़्यादा पैसा बचता है।
